evidence: ingest writes the cursor and fold from one refold result, so a losing writer's stale cursor is stored with its own fold covering exactly [0, cursor); the next refold folds [Ca, end) onto Fa, which lacks those bytes, so nothing is counted twice. The agent's 73d5bbd test (two overlapping different-mtime ingests then a settle read equals the from-scratch 0.06) pins it; the kernel was the imprecise 'cursor never rewinds' comment, which the agent corrected.

After the PR MetricsProvider no longer reads through parseJsonlFile, so a title naming 'the shared parse cache' described a mechanism the test no longer exercises; 73d5bbd renamed it and rewrote the body comment to name the mtime gate.
guidance_note: When a refactor removes the mechanism a test is named after, rename the test and its comments in the same commit that removes the mechanism.

evidence: The original reset was `size < priorOffset`, so a rewrite that grew back to >= the cursor would splice new-file suffix bytes onto the old fold; 73d5bbd added the inode to the cursor and resets on `ino !== prior.ino || size < prior.offset`, with a rename-rewrite test.
guidance_note: When a cache keys freshness on a byte offset into a file, enumerate every way the file can stop being an extension of the prefix (rename, truncate, truncate-and-regrow) before choosing the reset signal.

evidence: The assertion called `line(new Date(), 0.09)` a second time, which bumps the seq counter, so it passed only because the lengths happened to be equal; 73d5bbd captures `compacted` and asserts against its byteLength.
guidance_note: Assert against the exact value that was written, captured in a variable, never against a regenerated copy from a stateful helper.

evidence: The connect timer called `finish("econnrefused")`, which merged 'alive but backlog saturated' with the kernel ECONNREFUSED that the error handler reports; 73d5bbd added a distinct `connect_timeout` outcome and a pass clause for it.
guidance_note: In a diagnostic harness, give every distinct failure cause its own outcome variant rather than reusing the nearest existing label.

evidence: stateRoot and transcriptDir were created before spawnDaemon and removed only on the success path; 73d5bbd wrapped main in try/finally. The fix left `handle.cleanup()` inside the try, which produced F11/F22 in the next round.
guidance_note: When moving cleanup into a finally, list every resource the function acquires (temp dirs, child process, XDG dirs) and release all of them there, not only the ones the finding named.

evidence: The repeated stat plus ENOENT open per render is real, but the fast-hit gate is `mtime !== 0 && prior.cursor.mtimeMs === mtime` and an absent file stats to 0, so the proposed placeholder could never hit; the cost is bounded and stops once the file appears. Flag false positive: 73d5bbd touched only the metrics test title/comment, not the absent path, which predates review.

The reviewer conceded the behavior is correct (an evicted prior just means one whole-file refold) and asked only for documentation, and 556775b added that comment. Flag false positive: the thunk reading `this.entries.get(sessionId)` at run time predates review; 73d5bbd only rewrote the adjacent race comment.

The sync statSync bypasses the async gate on purpose (a single metadata stat that has to resolve before deciding whether to read). The reviewer offered 'or document why sync is safe', and 556775b did that on the one shared helper in transcript-fs. Flag false positive: statMtimeMs in metrics.ts predates review and 73d5bbd did not touch it.
guidance_note: When a new hot-path I/O call deliberately bypasses an established gate, put a comment saying why at the call site in the original PR.

evidence: foldMetrics' own incremental path had no test of append behavior, and 556775b added one that appends a user line (+1) and then an assistant line (unchanged). That test asserted only messageCount and left the recent ring unpinned, which produced F32. Flag false positive: the gap predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When adding a test for an incremental fold, assert every field the fold maintains (here messageCount and the recent ring via lastResponseTime), not just the one the reviewer mentioned.

evidence: 73d5bbd's F6 fix added a finally that removes only stateRoot and transcriptDir and left `handle.cleanup()` inside the try. Its own comment says spawnDaemon 'tears down its own child...on failure', which does not cover a throw after spawn succeeds. 556775b moved `handle?.cleanup()` into the finally.
guidance_note: When writing a finally for one leaked resource, sweep every acquisition between the try start and the success-path release, including the daemon handle.

evidence: `await fh?.close()` in finally would replace the ok() Outcome with a raw rejection that callers' `.kind` checks never see. The agent fixed both readAppended and readTail, but with the reviewer's `.catch(() => {})` and no log, which F39 then flagged. Flag false positive: the close-in-finally predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When suppressing an error so it cannot override a result, log it at the suppression point rather than applying an empty catch, especially under a no-silent-failure comment.

evidence: The reviewer said the old getSessionUsageFromPath set costUSD to the priced value before bucketByDay ran. The agent replied the divergence was 'PRE-EXISTING' and only reworded the comment. In F37 the agent admitted, after checking git history, that the old code did mutate entry.costUSD, so `today` had silently stopped pricing un-costed entries. Flag false positive: foldFile's day logic predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: Before pushing back with 'this behavior is pre-existing', read the deleted code in git history (here getSessionUsageFromPath's mutation of entry.costUSD) instead of reasoning from memory of it.

evidence: refold now runs on every mtime change, and findAgentTranscripts read each sidechain whole just to check its first line. 556775b passes the prior file set so already-verified sidechains skip the read. Flag false positive: findAgentTranscripts was not touched by 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When converting a per-miss path into a per-render path, audit every call inside it for O(file) work, not only the main read being made incremental.

evidence: parseJsonlLines skips lines where `!line.trim()` is true, and JSON.parse accepts surrounding whitespace on each line, so dropping the whole-content trim() changes no output. The reviewer itself wrote 'No semantic difference for valid inputs'. Flag false positive: claude.ts parse code predates 73d5bbd's cursor change.

This duplicates F13. The session/day divergence was real and introduced by this PR (shown in F37: the old code priced entry.costUSD in place before bucketing), but the agent resolved it as 'pre-existing' with a comment edit. Flag false positive: the day logic predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When two derived totals from the same entries diverge after a refactor, diff them against the deleted implementation before calling the divergence intended.

evidence: The store and metrics each had their own copy of statMtimeMs with the same ENOENT-to-0 policy; 556775b replaced both with one export from transcript-fs. Flag false positive: both copies predate 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: Before adding a second module that needs an existing private helper, export the first one rather than copying it.

evidence: The fast-hit returned `prior.recent` by reference. 556775b copied it there only, and its comment says 'the miss path already does', which is false: the miss path returns the stored `recent` itself. The unswept absent and miss paths became F33 and F35. Flag false positive: the hit path predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When fixing a reference-escape on one return path, check every return of the same field in the function, and check any claim about sibling paths before writing it into a comment.

evidence: `Number('abc')` gives NaN, and `Array.from({length: NaN})` gives [], so the harness ran zero sessions and passed. 556775b added posInt validation, but the pass condition could still pass with zero samples (interval > duration), which became F29. Flag false positive: arg parsing predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When closing one 'measured nothing yet passed' path, make the pass predicate itself require a non-empty sample, so no input combination can produce a vacuous pass.

evidence: onFrame ignored the frame, so `{ok:false}` responses were counted as fast 'ok' samples; 556775b added a render_error outcome and a pass clause. It did not sweep the remaining `other` outcome into pass, which became F28. Flag false positive: the frame handler predates 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When adding one failure outcome to a pass gate, check that every non-ok outcome variant in the union appears in the gate.

evidence: Both loadtest scripts default to `--daemon dist`, which needs dist/index.mjs, and on a clean checkout the run times out after 8s; 556775b added preloadtest and preloadtest:gate running pnpm build. Flag false positive: the scripts predate 73d5bbd.
guidance_note: When adding a script that depends on a build artifact, add its pre-hook in the same change.

evidence: This duplicates F11: the F6 fix in 73d5bbd left `handle.cleanup()` in the try, so a throw after spawn orphans the daemon child and its XDG dirs. 556775b moved it into the finally.
guidance_note: When writing a finally for one leaked resource, release every resource acquired in the guarded span, the child process included.

evidence: 73d5bbd added inode-change as a second reset signal, but CLAUDE.md still called 'file shrinks below the cursor' 'the one reset case'. 556775b updated CLAUDE.md to name both signals.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a documented contract (here the reset conditions), grep CLAUDE.md and the docs for the old description and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The same-inode in-place rewrite to >= cursor is a real gap, but the reviewer conceded /compact renames (caught by the inode check), and a prefix hash would add a read per render, against the O(appended) goal. Flag false positive: this is the residual the agent named and declined in its F3 reply, which existed before review; 556775b did not change the reset logic.
guidance_note: When deliberately leaving a known residual, state the excluded case explicitly in the code comment at the check so a reviewer reading it sees a decision, not an oversight.

evidence: The read buffer is `Buffer.alloc(size - start)`, sized from the same stat, so removing the `start >= size` guard could never capture bytes appended after the stat; the next render's mtime gate picks them up. Flag false positive: the guard predates 556775b.

foldFile awaits PricingService.calculateCostForEntry with no catch, so a pricing throw becomes a rejected promise past every Outcome caller; the deleted getSessionUsageFromPath caught this. 3ce854e wraps flight.run in try/catch returning failed(). Flag false positive: this regression dates from the original PR, not 556775b.
guidance_note: When deleting a function that wrapped a body in try/catch to keep an Outcome contract total, carry that catch over to whatever replaces it in the same PR.

evidence: The metrics fast-hit did not re-insert the session into the Map, so its LRU order reflected writes only, while the usage store's hit path re-orders; 3ce854e added delete+set on the hit. Flag false positive: the hit path's ordering predates 556775b (that commit only added the copy).
guidance_note: When building a second LRU cache modeled on an existing one, mirror every touch point of the original, the hit-path re-order included.

evidence: 556775b's F20 fix added `render_error === 0` to the pass gate but left the `other` outcome (framing errors, EMFILE) out. 3ce854e added `byOutcome("other") === 0`.
guidance_note: When adding one failure outcome to a pass gate, check that every non-ok outcome variant in the union appears in the gate.

evidence: posInt (the F19 fix) rejects NaN but accepts interval > duration, which still yields zero samples, and pct([]) returns 0, so the gate passed vacuously. 3ce854e added `steady.length > 0`, and the agent verified that `--interval 5000 --duration 2` now gives PASS false.
guidance_note: When closing one 'measured nothing yet passed' path, make the pass predicate itself require a non-empty sample, so no input combination can produce a vacuous pass.

evidence: profileDir comes from mkdtempSync and appears in no cleanup path, so a failed --profile run leaves an empty dir behind; 3ce854e removes it when it holds no profiles. Flag false positive: profileDir creation predates 556775b.
guidance_note: When a function creates several temp dirs, list each one's owner and release path at creation time.

evidence: `Math.floor((p/100)*N)` returns the max for p99 at N=100; 3ce854e switched to nearest-rank `ceil(pN/100)-1`. Flag false positive: 73d5bbd only reformatted pct and its logic predates review.
guidance_note: Use a named standard percentile definition (nearest-rank) in a gate, and check it by hand at N=1, 2 and 100.

evidence: The incremental test added for F10 in 556775b asserted only messageCount, so the recent ring that feeds lastResponseTime was unpinned. 3ce854e added lastResponseTime assertions (null, then about 1.0s).
guidance_note: When adding a test for an incremental fold, assert every field the fold maintains, not just the one the finding named.

evidence: 556775b's F18 fix copied `recent` on the fast-hit, but the absent path still returned `prior?.recent ?? []` by reference. f7ec991 copied it there too.
guidance_note: When fixing a reference-escape on one return path, check every return of the same field in the function.

evidence: In the diff the warmup loop is `await Promise.all(sessions.map((s) => oneRender(...)))` with the results discarded; only the measurement setInterval does `.then((sample) => samples.push(sample))`. So samples.length and elapsedS cover the same window. Flag false positive: 3ce854e did not touch the sampling code.

The miss path does `this.state.set(sessionId, {..., recent})` and then returns the same `recent`. The F18 comment ('the miss path already does') and the F33 comment in f7ec991 ('like the hit/miss paths') both claimed it copied. Fixed in 2f953c5, which also corrected the comment. This is the third round on one field.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that claims a sibling code path already does something, read that path; two fix rounds repeated the same false claim here.

evidence: The reviewer conceded callers gate on mtime before calling readAppendedEntries and that the unchanged-file path is covered indirectly. A direct test that a prior cursor on an unchanged file yields zero entries is cheap and pins the reader's contract, and 2f953c5 added it. Flag false positive: f7ec991 touched only metrics.ts.

The 'PRE-EXISTING' comment that 556775b wrote for F13/F16 was false: the agent conceded 'you were right, I was wrong', having checked git history that getSessionUsageFromPath mutated costUSD before bucketByDay. 2f953c5 prices the day bucket and adds a test that today equals the session's priced cost. F13's response fixed only the wording and left the regression in place.
guidance_note: Before pushing back with 'this behavior is pre-existing', read the deleted code in git history instead of reasoning from memory of it.

evidence: This is the third raising of the same-inode in-place-rewrite residual (after F3 and F24). The reviewer again called it 'narrow and unlikely', and catching it would need a per-render prefix read, which defeats the O(appended) design. Flag false positive: f7ec991 did not touch transcript-fs.
guidance_note: When a residual is deliberately left, put the exact excluded case in the comment at the check so later review rounds do not re-raise it.

evidence: 556775b's F12 fix was `await fh?.close().catch(() => {})`, under a comment labeled [LAW:no-silent-failure], and it discards the close error with no log. 2f953c5 logs it at debug in both readAppended and readTail.
guidance_note: When suppressing an error so it cannot override a result, log it at the suppression point; an empty catch under a no-silent-failure comment contradicts itself.

evidence: The reviewer itself says it is 'not a correctness bug' and 'transient and benign'. The offset only advances past complete lines, and a completing write bumps mtime, so the next render re-reads from the same offset. Flag false positive: f7ec991 did not touch claude.ts.

With `void main()`, a throw skips `process.exit(exitCode)`. Modern Node already exits non-zero on an unhandled rejection, so the risk was overstated, but an explicit `.catch` that exits 1 is the clearer contract. Flag false positive: `void main()` predates review, and f7ec991 did not touch the harness.
guidance_note: When a script entry point is async, add an explicit catch that exits non-zero in the original PR.

evidence: This is the fourth temp-dir/child leak path in this harness (F6, F11/F22, F30). The XDG cache and config dirs are created before spawn(), so a spawn throw leaves `handle` null and the dirs leak. The F30 fix in 3ce854e edited spawnDaemon's cleanup but did not cover the spawn-throw path. Fixed in 2f953c5.
guidance_note: When fixing a leak in a function that acquires several temp resources, trace every throw site between acquisition and handle return, not only the path the finding named.

narrative: This was a large perf PR, and 42 findings over five rounds came almost all from advisory-heavy CoPirate reviews. Most findings were real and fixed in one pass, and the agent's pushbacks on F1, F15, F25, F34 and F40 were correct on the code. Ten findings were caused by earlier fixes that did not sweep sibling instances: the harness cleanup took four rounds (F6 to F11/F22 to F30 to F42), and the recent-ring copy took three (F18 to F33 to F35), with the agent twice writing a false comment that the miss path already copied. The worst miss was F13/F16: the agent called the day-cost divergence pre-existing without checking the deleted code, and wrote that claim into a comment; F37 then forced a retraction and the real fix. Round 4 exists only because of the F18/F33 copy fix (f7ec991).
guidance_observations: The agent twice wrote comments claiming a sibling code path already behaved correctly (F18 and F33) without reading it; each false claim became a later finding.
On a pushback that rests on historical behavior ('pre-existing'), the agent reasoned from memory instead of checking git history, and only did that check one round later when challenged again (F37).
The harness fixes each covered exactly the path the finding named; listing every acquired resource and every throw site once would have closed F11, F22, F30 and F42 in the first fix.

Pass-gate fixes added one outcome clause at a time (connect_timeout, render_error, other, non-empty) instead of deriving the gate from the full outcome union plus a non-empty requirement in one change.
